lessons.text: queue dev ai try runs commands via exec and does not inherit the sourced shell function named queue. When testing queue subcommands from a source-tree checkout, wrap the attempt as timeout N bash -lc 'cd TREE; export QUEUEBASH_ALLOW_NONINTERACTIVE=1; source ./queuebash.sh; queue ...' so it is both sourced and bounded.

queue dev ai try is intentionally allowlisted; timeout bash -lc wrappers may be rejected as command_not_allowlisted even though they are the right operational pattern for manual bounded queue-function probes. Use try for allowlisted validations such as bash -n, and record direct bounded queue probes as lessons/evidence.
0.18.92 external signed display resources merge preserved queuebash.sh shell syntax; queue dev ai try allowlisted 'bash -n queuebash.sh' and recorded a pass.

Some queue smoke tests source queuebash.sh and trigger bundled policy/resource installation, so short 20-45s timeouts can falsely kill valid tests in the sandbox. For queue_command_json_wave3_smoke.sh use a bounded but realistic timeout such as 180s; direct 'timeout queue ...' cannot see shell functions, so use bash -lc with source when probing functions.
